title: Linear Cech comparison through a flasque computing resolution
statement: Let $U_i$ cover a scheme $X$, and let $D$ be a computing resolution of an $\mathcal O_X$-module $F$ [def-sc-module-cup-resolution-data] with flasque terms [def-sc-zariski-flasque]. Alpha [def-sc-cup-cech-total] is a quasi-isomorphism. For every $n\ge0$, every canonical comparison $c:\check H^n(U,F)\to H^n(X,F)$ [def-sc-module-cech-comparison], coefficient Cech kernel cocycle $a$ and global resolution kernel cocycle $b$, the equation $H^n(\alpha)([b])=H^n(\beta)([a])$ implies $D.class(n,b)=c([a])$. This is a one-module linear comparison, with no section pairing or cup product.

source.place: Tags 01EQ and 0FKV, linear comparison along the flasque alpha diagram

proof.text: In positive degrees apply the proved source theorem TopCat.Sheaf.exactAt_cechComplex_of_isFlasque to each underlying abelian sheaf. Transport its zero homology through TopCat.Presheaf.cechComplexFunctorHomologyIso. Forgetting a module reflects zero objects, and the source single complex also has zero positive homology; hence the row augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism there.

In degree zero a Cech cocycle is a compatible tuple of sections: evaluate its differential on each pair to obtain equality on the overlap. The sheaf gluing axiom provides a unique section on the union, which is the whole space by the covering equation. Restriction to tuples is injective by sheaf uniqueness and surjective onto the kernel by this gluing. There are no degree-zero boundaries. The identity scalar-restriction isomorphism identifies this map with the augmentation, proving its degree-zero quasi-isomorphism.

Apply the first-quadrant column-augmentation criterion to the flipped double complex and the complex of global sections. The column augmentations just proved are quasi-isomorphisms. The signed total-flip isomorphism carries the resulting augmentation to cupCechAlpha; on the (n,0) axis its sign is one.

Apply the Cech functor and totalization to D.comparison. Naturality of restriction gives the alpha square termwise. D.over gives the beta square on degree-zero resolution components, by functoriality of Cech. These squares and the assumed equality identify H(alpha for D.I) applied to the global comparison image of [b] with H(beta for D.I)([a]).

The defining canonical comparison equation evaluated on D.I identifies that same beta image with H(alpha for D.I) of the injective resolution identification of c([a]). Cancel H(alpha for D.I), which is invertible by moduleCechAlpha_isIso. Apply the inverse injective-resolution identification to obtain precisely D.class(n,b)=c([a]).

theorem cupCech_flasque_comparison {X : Scheme.{u}} {ι : Type u}
    (U : ι → X.Opens) (hU : iSup U = ⊤) {F : X.Modules}
    (D : CupAcyclicResolution F)
    (hD : ∀ n : ℕ, TopCat.Sheaf.IsFlasque
      ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)).obj (D.K.X n))) :
    QuasiIso (cupCechAlpha U D) ∧
    ∀ (n : ℕ)
      (c : ((cechComplexFunctor U).obj F.presheafModuleCat).homology n ⟶
        (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology X.toRingedSpace n).obj F),
      IsModuleCechComparison U F n c →
      ∀ (a : (((cechComplexFunctor U).obj F.presheafModuleCat).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (b : ((cupSections D).sc n).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K),
        HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (cupCechAlpha U D) n (cupCycleClass _ n b) =
          HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (cupCechBeta U D) n (cupCycleClass _ n a) →
        D.class n b = c (cupCycleClass _ n a)
